svg.font-family: Segoe UI, Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: System lifecycle — the states the whole app shares, and where a user gets stuck
svg.desc: States are combinations of facts, not screens: a rootfs on disk, health, whether the server answers, and who holds the environment lock. Edges are labelled with the guard that allows them, cited to file:line. Red states are dead ends. Read this before drawing any per-area diagram, and reuse these state names verbatim.
svg.text: System lifecycle — where a user gets stuck
A state is a combination of facts, never a screen. Verified against the working tree, 13 Aug — after ADFA-5137 deleted setup_complete. Every edge cites the guard that allows it.

DEAD ENDS, WORST FIRST — traps, then one-way doors, then exits nobody can find, then controls that do nothing

Ranked by how hard the state is to escape, not by how ugly it looks. As of 14 Aug: findings 1, 3, 5 and 8 are closed, and 4 lost one of its three blind spots. Finding 8 was found by using the app, not by reading it — and one of its claims turned out to be wrong for the same reason.
Findings 1, 2, 3 and 4 are one sentence four times: a fact nobody clears. They are rows in the standing directive's ledger at the top of operation-model-roadmap.svg — fix them there, not here.
1 · CLOSED (13 Aug, ADFA-5119) — the boot gate no longer holds an install nobody can influence
Was: the installing branch had no safety timer, so the gate lifted only on a terminal state — and a run that stopped reporting kept its own foreground process alive
while InstallProgressRepository still said "running". Force-stop was the only exit, and it does not clear the install marker, so the next launch landed in recovery.
Now the download leg cannot go quiet. A transfer that stops moving is caught in ten seconds by our own watchdog — aria2 keeps the download open at 0 B/s and never
reports it — retried three times in the open, then held with Retry and Cancel on screen; unattended, the held state expires after a minute into recovery.
Aria2Manager (stall watchdog, Stop.STALL) · InstallService (softFail, the held window, forgetTheAbandonedSystem, teardown keeps the marker) · LibraryActivity (Pause/Retry/Cancel, FAILED → recovery).

Closed FOR THE DOWNLOAD LEG, which is the one that holds the gate on a first install. Two things behind it are not: verify, extract and provisioning have no watchdog and are deliberately offered no controls, so a genuine hang there

is still a trap — rarer, and unbounded. And the kiwix index (:478-479) and maps (:545-546) still send exit AND error onward, so a failed companion run reports as a finished install. Maps → ADFA-4898, the rest under ADFA-4893.
2 · HIDDEN EXIT — a stale "busy" flag refuses every deep operation, and the way out has no name
A download service killed before reaching a terminal state leaves EnvironmentLock.isBusyNow() true. Clone, backup, restore, module install and the dashboard rebuild
all refuse, all with the same message — "An install is already running" — while nothing is running. It is not durable: every source it reads is in-memory, so closing
the app clears it. That is the whole problem. The exit exists and nobody will find it, because no one closes an app to unblock a button.
env/EnvironmentLock.java:69-87 (all four sources are process-scoped), 97-100 (the file names this and points at ADFA-4874).

ADFA-5146. An age past which a session is ignored, and a message that names what is actually holding the lock. The expiry needs only an in-memory timestamp, not the durable record — the stale flag dies with the process, so 4897 is a different problem.
3 · CLOSED (13 Aug, ADFA-5137) — the flag that could disagree with reality no longer exists
Was: setup_complete was written when an install STARTED, and by "Copy from a phone" before a transfer existed, and cleared by nobody. So a failed install, a failed clone,
or a reinstall that destroyed the rootfs without finishing, all landed in S1 — and from there the app routed to the Library forever and never offered the wizard again.
ADFA-5119 closed the install route: a failure keeps the install marker and lands in recovery. ADFA-5137 removed the flag outright. The launch now asks whether a rootfs, an
install or a deep operation is there — three facts that each die with the thing they describe — so the four writers and four readers went with it. Four boolean facts allow
sixteen combinations; three allow eight, and all eight describe something physically true. The dead end is not fixed, it is unrepresentable.
system/domain/SystemPresence (the rule, eight-row truth table) · system/data/SystemFactsReader.hereOrOnTheWay (the three reads) · the preference key is gone from 34 files.
Ledger consequence: the setup_complete row is deleted rather than turned green. The first row of the standing directive's own table stops existing.
4 · CLOSED (14 Aug, ADFA-5147) — a damaged system is now diagnosed where it is shown, not only in the launch branch
Was: the recovery dialog ran only on the "recovering" branch. A held lock, a running install or module queue skipped it, the user landed on Home, and the install
marker forced isSystemInstalled() false — so a damaged system read as "no system": no dialog, no mention of damage. Now Home asks InterruptedInstallDetector, the
same owner the launch dialog uses, and shows H_DAMAGED — "Library needs repair" with a Recover action — so the diagnosis no longer depends on which door was taken.
LibraryHomeFragment.updateHeaderFromCards (the !installed branch) + H_DAMAGED · InterruptedInstallDetector.evaluate · SystemStateEvaluator.isSystemInstalled.
Device-verified: a killed clone reached through recovery → wizard → clone lands on Home saying "needs repair", not "no library". Scope was the diagnosis; the surfaces a
systemless user can still wander (the module sheet, Add-modules, Connect) are findings 5 and 7, now owned by ADFA-5150 and ADFA-5151.
5 · CLOSED (13 Aug, ADFA-5137) — the state is unrepresentable now, and the screen was given an exit anyway
The entrance went with finding 3. S1 needed setup_complete to disagree with the disk, and there is no flag left to disagree with anything: a device with nothing on it now
opens the wizard. Phones already stuck in S1 — including anyone who used the Skip that ADFA-5116 removed — are freed on their next launch, with no migration.
The screen was fixed too, deliberately and not for belt and braces. H_NO_LIBRARY was the one header state offering nothing while FAILED offers Retry and INSTALLING offers
See progress; it now offers "Install a system", routing through openGetMore(), which re-reads the facts at click time and refuses while a deep operation holds the lock.
Both halves, because a reused LibraryActivity instance never re-runs the launch check — onNewIntent skips it — so "no system on Home" stays reachable for an instance that
was already alive. A state with no exit is a bug whoever reaches it, including by a route that does not exist yet.
LibraryHomeFragment:111 (the action), :252-275 (openGetMore — re-read + ownerHeld guard) · LibraryActivity:112-127 (the launch check) · ModuleHubFragment:232-243.
6 · DEAD CONTROL — a banked order that is not running is invisible and, for three types, uncancellable
"See progress" appears only while something is actually running, and a refused or deferred drain leaves the order banked without running. Nothing lists it. The module
sheet's Cancel is the only cancel in the app, and it only inspects the maps and module wishlists — a banked ZIM, Books or Courses order cannot be cancelled from
anywhere in the UI.
LibraryHomeFragment.java:518-529 (anyRunning gates the button), :337-342 (isScheduled ignores three of the five wishlists).
7 · DEAD CONTROL — Connect hands out a QR for a box that may not exist
ConnectFragment reads no system fact at all: not isSystemInstalled, not the server state, not the lock. With no system, a damaged one, or the server stopped, the whole
tab behaves normally and prints a QR pointing at a dead port. It is the largest visible-but-useless surface in the app, and the only one that says nothing at all about
why it will not work.
redesign/ConnectFragment.java — browseUrl():126; no reference to SystemFacts, ServerStateRepository or EnvironmentLock anywhere in the file.
8 · CLOSED — a clone in flight said the system had failed to start, and offered no way back to the transfer
The server is stopped on purpose while a clone runs. The header read !alive and, with no start in progress, concluded H_FAILED — "Couldn't start — tap to retry" — so it
stated something false about a perfectly healthy device, and the only route back into the transfer was to remember which tab it lived in. Now H_CLONE_RECEIVING and
H_CLONE_SHARING are asked before "is anything installed", so a clone in flight has its own amber state and its action returns to the Clone tab.
One claim written here was wrong and is worth keeping visible: that the Retry would boot the server on top of a live transfer. It would not — handleServerLaunchClick
refuses while EnvironmentLock.ownerHeld, and the guard was already there. The dead control was a lie on the header, not a destructive one, and it was ranked one
priority too high until the code was read instead of inferred.
LibraryHomeFragment.H_CLONE_RECEIVING/H_CLONE_SHARING · LibraryActivity.canStartServer() · openCloneTab() · CloneFragment.showReceiveTerminal().
ADFA-5143, with the recovery loop and the ownership release. Leftover: the release runs when the UI reaches the terminal, so a receive whose tab is never reopened still keeps the marker.
